documents.title: Interim arrangements during the Harbor Street renovation
documents.text:
To: All Finance and Procurement staff
From: Daniela Okafor, Facilities Coordinator
Date: 14 March

As you know, the renovation of the fourth floor at Harbor Street begins on 1 April and is expected to last roughly ten weeks. Rather than relocating everyone to a rented site, management has opted for a phased approach, which means that desks will be reassigned in stages and some of you will be asked to work remotely for part of the period.

Employees whose surnames begin with A through L will keep their current seats until 15 April, after which they will move to the second floor. Those with surnames from M to Z will work from home during the first five weeks and return on 6 May, when the new workstations are scheduled to be ready. Anyone who cannot work from home for practical reasons, for instance because of unreliable internet access, should contact me before 21 March so that a temporary desk can be reserved in the ground-floor library.

Please note that the print room will be closed throughout the works. Documents that must be signed physically should be scanned and routed through the electronic approval system instead. Packing materials will be delivered to each team leader on 28 March, and every box must be labeled with the owner's name and destination floor. Items left unlabeled will be stored but may take considerably longer to retrieve.

choices: To announce that a department will be moved to a rented site
To explain how staff will be housed during building work
To ask employees to volunteer for a trial of remote working
To justify why a renovation budget has been exceeded
questions.explanation: The memo describes a phased approach with seat reassignments and remote work during the renovation. No rented site is used, no volunteers are sought and no budget is mentioned.

choices: In the middle of April

In the first week of May
questions.explanation: Surnames from M to Z work from home for five weeks and return on 6 May. 'Novak' begins with N, so early May applies.

choices: Ask for a temporary place to work by a set date

Order their packing materials in advance
Use the print room as an alternative site
questions.explanation: The memo says to contact the coordinator before 21 March so that a temporary desk can be reserved in the library.

questions.prompt: According to the memo, what could happen to boxes without a label?
choices: They will be thrown away after the move
They will be sent to the wrong team leader
They may be slow to reach their owners again
They will be opened and checked by security
questions.explanation: Unlabeled items 'will be stored but may take considerably longer to retrieve', so retrieval will be slow. Nothing suggests disposal, misdelivery or inspection.

documents.title: Quiet revival of the neighborhood bakery
documents.text:
Over the past decade, industrial bakeries and supermarket in-store ovens have taken the lion's share of bread sales across the region. Yet in several mid-sized towns, independent bakers are reporting a modest but unmistakable comeback. According to a survey published by the Regional Artisan Food Council, the number of registered neighborhood bakeries rose by six percent last year, the first increase since 2009.

Analysts attribute the shift to a combination of factors. Consumers who work from home are shopping closer to their residences and are willing to pay more for loaves that are baked on the premises. Meanwhile, rising energy costs, which once threatened to push small producers out of business, have eased thanks to a subsidy program for efficient ovens. Several bakers interviewed said the subsidy allowed them to replace equipment that was more than twenty years old.

Not everyone is convinced the trend will last. Marcus Telford, who runs the Millstone Loaf in Dunmore, cautions that skilled apprentices are scarce. "People love the idea of a baker on every corner," he says, "but few young people want to start work at three in the morning." Without a steady supply of trained staff, he argues, new shops could close as quickly as they opened. The Council has responded by proposing a paid training scheme that would be piloted in three towns next autumn.

questions.prompt: What is the article mainly about?
choices: The decline of supermarkets in small towns
A new technique for baking bread more efficiently
A tentative recovery among independent bread-makers
A dispute over public support for local farmers
questions.explanation: The article reports a modest comeback of neighborhood bakeries after years of dominance by industrial producers. Supermarkets, baking methods and farmers are not the focus.

questions.prompt: What has helped small bakers deal with energy costs?
choices: Public money for buying more economical machinery
A fall in the price of flour on the market
An agreement with a supplier of electricity
Longer opening hours at the weekend
questions.explanation: A subsidy program for efficient ovens eased the burden, allowing bakers to replace old equipment.

questions.prompt: The word "cautions" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
choices: advises against buying
forgives
negotiates
warns
questions.explanation: Mr. Telford says the trend may not last because of a lack of apprentices, so he is giving a warning.

questions.prompt: What does Mr. Telford suggest about the future of new bakeries?
choices: Most will merge with larger regional firms
Some may fail for lack of qualified employees
They will gain from a shortage of supermarkets
They will stop selling bread early in the morning
questions.explanation: He argues that without a steady supply of trained staff, new shops 'could close as quickly as they opened'.

documents.title: Notice to residents of Fenwick Court
documents.text:
Notice to all residents of Fenwick Court

Following the inspection carried out in February, the management company has scheduled the replacement of the building's central water heating system. [A] The work will be carried out between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. on weekdays from 8 to 19 May, and hot water will be unavailable on the days indicated below for each wing. [B] Residents of the east wing will be affected on 8, 9 and 12 May, while those in the west wing will be without hot water on 13, 14 and 15 May. The north wing will be done last, on 16 and 19 May.

Because the contractor will need access to the boiler room in the basement, the bicycle storage area will be closed for the entire period. [C] Owners are asked to remove their bicycles by 5 May; any bicycle remaining after that date will be moved to the courtyard, and the management company cannot be held liable for damage or theft.

A free shower facility will be available at the Lindqvist Sports Center, a five-minute walk from the building, upon presentation of a resident card. [D] Residents who are elderly or have limited mobility may request a portable water heater by calling the office before 30 April. We apologize for the inconvenience and thank you for your patience.

questions.prompt: Why was the notice written?
choices: To invite residents to attend a safety inspection
To warn residents of a planned service interruption
To announce a rise in the monthly charges
To recruit volunteers for a building committee
questions.explanation: The notice schedules the replacement of the heating system and lists the days when hot water will be unavailable.

questions.prompt: When will the north wing be without hot water?
choices: During the first week of the work
Only at the weekend, outside work hours
Between 13 and 15 May, with the west wing
On the final two days of the project
questions.explanation: The north wing will be done last, on 16 and 19 May, which are the final days of the schedule.

questions.prompt: What are bicycle owners asked to do?
choices: Clear the storage area before a deadline
Pay a fee for leaving bikes in the courtyard
Register their bicycles at the management office
Wait until the contractor has left the boiler room
questions.explanation: Owners must remove bicycles by 5 May because the storage area will be closed.

questions.prompt: In which position marked [A], [B], [C] or [D] does the following sentence best belong? "Anyone with a health condition should make arrangements with the office in advance."
questions.explanation: The sentence fits after the shower facility information, just before the text about residents with limited mobility who must call before 30 April. [D] is the only position where it introduces that point.

Haruto Mizuno (10:02): Hello, I purchased the team license last week, but only three of my colleagues can sign in. We paid for ten seats.
Sandra Lowe, Ardent Support (10:04): Good morning, Mr. Mizuno. Let me check your account. Could you confirm the e-mail address used for the purchase?

Sandra Lowe (10:08): Thank you. I can see the order, but the seats have not been assigned yet. The system only activates a seat once the administrator invites a user by e-mail, and so far three invitations have been sent.

documents.title: Logistics Planner, Corvane Freight (Rotterdam)
documents.text:
Corvane Freight, a European provider of road and sea transport, is looking for a Logistics Planner to join its Rotterdam operations team. Reporting to the Head of Operations, you will coordinate weekly schedules for about forty drivers and liaise with port authorities and customers on a daily basis.

Requirements: at least three years in a similar role; fluency in English and Dutch (German is an advantage); experience with route-optimization software; the ability to make decisions quickly when shipments are disrupted. A degree in supply chain management is welcome but not essential for candidates with strong practical experience.

We offer a permanent contract, a flexible schedule with two remote days per week after the probation period of six months, and a yearly learning budget of 1,500 euros. Applications, including a cover letter, should reach Ms. Ilse de Wit (hr@corvanefreight.example) before 30 June. Shortlisted candidates will be asked to complete a short planning exercise during the interview.

documents.title: Application: Logistics Planner
documents.text:
Dear Ms. de Wit,

I am writing to apply for the Logistics Planner position advertised on your website. For the past four years I have worked at Nordhaven Shipping in Hamburg, where I schedule deliveries for a fleet of thirty-five trucks and am the first contact for customs agents when a container is held up. Last year I led the introduction of a route-planning tool that shortened average delivery times by eleven percent, and I have since trained eight colleagues to use it.

Although I do not hold a degree in logistics, I completed a professional certificate in transport management two years ago. I speak English and German fluently and am currently taking Dutch lessons; I can hold a conversation but would need a few months to work comfortably in writing. I would be willing to relocate to Rotterdam at my own expense and could start on 1 September, since my notice period is two months.

My résumé is attached. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience could benefit your team.

Sincerely,
Tobias Brandt

documents.title: Re: Application: Logistics Planner
documents.text:
Dear Mr. Brandt,

Thank you for your application, which we read with interest. Your experience with route planning is very close to what the team needs, and the committee was especially struck by the figure you gave for faster deliveries. We would like to invite you for an interview on Thursday 17 July at our Rotterdam office; if you cannot travel, a video call can be arranged. As mentioned in the advertisement, you will be given a planning exercise, which usually takes about forty-five minutes.

Regarding language, our customers in the Netherlands communicate mainly in Dutch, so we would be glad to cover the cost of a course should you join us. Please confirm your availability by Monday.

Kind regards,
Ilse de Wit

questions.explanation: The ad says the planner will liaise with port authorities and customers daily. The contract is permanent and a degree is not essential.

documents.title: Harlow Valley Cooperative Market: Membership drive
documents.text: Join the Harlow Valley Cooperative Market and shop for local, seasonal produce at member prices. Members receive a 12 percent discount on every purchase, early access to our monthly specialty boxes, and a vote at the annual meeting where decisions about suppliers and store hours are made. Membership costs 40 dollars per year, or 25 dollars for students and seniors. Sign up at the customer service desk before 31 October and your first month's discount will be doubled. Our produce comes from farms within eighty kilometers of the store, and every supplier is visited by a member of our sourcing committee at least once a year.

documents.title: Re: Membership question
documents.text:
Dear Ms. Fowler,

Thank you for your inquiry. To answer your questions: yes, the fee is refundable within thirty days if you are not satisfied, but the discount and the early-access boxes can only be used while your membership is active. Because you mentioned that you are studying part-time, you may qualify for the reduced fee if you bring a valid student card. Please note that the offer for doubling the first month's discount ends on 31 October, so signing up on the day we speak would still qualify.

Our next specialty box, featuring autumn apples and cider, will be released to members on 3 November and to the public on 10 November. If you decide to join, I would recommend reserving it online, since the quantities are limited and previous boxes have sold out within two days.

Kind regards,
Rafael Ortiz

documents.title: Letter from the Allerton Arts Council
documents.text:
Dear Mr. Chen,

On behalf of the Allerton Arts Council, I am pleased to inform you that your application for the Emerging Studio grant has been successful. The selection committee, which reviewed nearly ninety proposals, was particularly impressed by your plan to turn the former textile mill into a shared workspace for ceramic artists.

The grant amounts to 18,000 dollars and will be paid in two installments. The first, 12,000 dollars, will be transferred once we receive the signed agreement enclosed with this letter. The remaining 6,000 dollars will be released after you submit a progress report, due no later than 15 January. We would also ask that you acknowledge the Council's support on all promotional material.

Please note that funds may only be used for equipment, materials and renovation costs; salaries are not covered. Should your plans change significantly, you are required to notify us in writing before making any related expenditure. Our office is also happy to put you in touch with previous recipients who have run shared studios and can share their experience of managing tenants and kiln schedules.

Sincerely,
Gwen Hatcher, Program Director

documents.title: Question about grant spending
documents.text:
Dear Ms. Hatcher,

Thank you for the wonderful news. Before returning the agreement, I have two questions. First, the mill's roof needs urgent repair, which will use up nearly a third of the first installment. I assume that falls under renovation costs. Second, we hope to hire a part-time studio assistant. If salaries are excluded, could we pay this person with income from the workshops we plan to run?

I would also like to know whether the progress report can be a short video rather than a written document, and whether you could introduce me to one of the previous recipients you mentioned. A conversation before the end of the month would be especially useful.

Best regards,
Li Chen

documents.title: Re: Question about grant spending
documents.text:
Dear Mr. Chen,

Roof repairs do count as renovation, so please go ahead. Wages may indeed come from income that is separate from the grant, as long as the two are accounted for separately in your report. The report may be a video, provided it is accompanied by a one-page summary of expenditure.

I have asked Emma Torres, who converted a former printing house in Dunmore, to contact you this week.

Regards,
Gwen Hatcher

choices: To request a progress report on a project

To notify an applicant of a funding decision
questions.explanation: The letter begins by telling Mr. Chen that his application was successful and then explains the terms.

documents.title: Equipment loan request form
documents.text:
Borrower: Sasha Petrov, Department of Biology
Item: Portable spectrometer (model PS-40)
Loan period requested: 12 to 23 June
Purpose: Fieldwork in the Vesna wetlands, water quality sampling
Return location: Science building, Room 112
Conditions: Borrowers are responsible for any damage. A deposit of 150 dollars is required and will be refunded within five working days of return, provided the device is undamaged. Late returns are charged 10 dollars per day. Devices must be collected from the equipment room in person during opening hours, which are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.

documents.title: Re: Loan request, PS-40
documents.text:
Hello Sasha,

I'm afraid the PS-40 is not available for the whole period you asked for, since another group has booked it from 20 June. I can offer you the PS-35, which is slightly older but measures the same parameters, for the full twelve days. The only difference is that the PS-35 has a battery life of six hours rather than ten, so you would need to bring a spare battery pack, which we can lend you at no additional deposit.

If you prefer to keep the PS-40, I can lend it from 12 to 19 June. Please let me know by Friday so I can update the form. Whichever model you choose, remember that the sensor must be calibrated before each field day, and a calibration kit is included with both devices.

Best,
Collins Reyes
Lab Technician

documents.title: Message from Sasha Petrov to Prof. Amara
documents.text: Hi Professor, the lab only has the older spectrometer for my full dates. It's fine for our parameters, but I'd have to return it on the 23rd by noon. Could you sign off on the deposit? I'm also thinking of cutting the trip to a week, since we might not need the last days. If I do that, I could keep the newer device after all. Will let you know tomorrow. The wetlands site has no power, so the spare battery would matter either way.
